collections.title: 2D Golden Geometry & Constructions
collections.enunciation: Planar compass-and-straightedge divisions in extreme and mean ratio, golden and root-5 rectangles with orthogonal gnomonic spiral poles, self-deflating golden triangles and gnomons, pentagonal star progressions and overhand paper-strip knots, Kepler's geometric-progression right triangle, and Penrose aperiodic P2/P3 prototiles.

collections.title: Exact Pentagonal & Constructible Trigonometry
collections.enunciation: Closed-form quadratic radicals and Rational Trigonometry spreads for 18°, 36°, 54°, and 72°, extended by Euclid IV.16 pentagon-equilateral superposition across all 29 constructible multiples of 3° in the first quadrant and contrasted with Gauss's Fermat-prime regular 17-gon cosine.

collections.title: 3D Golden Geometry of Solids
collections.enunciation: Three-dimensional golden coordinates spanning the regular icosahedron and dodecahedron from three mutually orthogonal golden rectangles, Euclid XIII.17's inscribed cube and five-cube compound, and the acute and obtuse golden rhombohedra of icosahedral quasicrystals.

collections.title: Algebraic Powers of Φ, Continued Fractions & Base-Φ Phigits
collections.enunciation: Linearization of all integer powers of Φ into Fibonacci multiples, the unit-volume Phibonacci brick, extremal continued fraction convergents F_{n+1}/F_n and Hurwitz's √5 irrationality barrier, and George Bergman's non-adjacent base-Φ ('phigit') numeral system.

collections.title: The Golden String, Zeckendorf Base, & Wythoff / Stolarsky Arrays
collections.enunciation: The infinite Sturmian Golden String (101101011011...) generated both by morphism substitution and by a lattice-cutting ray of slope φ, Zeckendorf's canonical non-consecutive Fibonacci base, and the bijective Beatty, Wythoff, and Stolarsky interspersion arrays.

collections.title: Fibonacci-Lucas Identities, Pythagorean Triples, Jigsaw Paradoxes & π
collections.enunciation: Four-term Fibonacci generators of Pythagorean right triangles, Cassini's alternating ±1 determinant realized as 64 ↔ 65 and 64 ↔ 63 four-piece dissections, Binet/Lucas/Catalan/d'Ocagne/Honsberger and Fibonomial power identities, Fibonacci arctangent telescoping series for π, and the Golden Angle parastichy lattice.

items.title: Internal & External Golden Section Constructions on a Segment
items.theorem_enunciation: Given a finite segment AB, midpoint-circle compass-and-straightedge constructions divide AB internally at G so AB : AG = AG : GB = Φ and extend AB externally to E so AE : AB = AB : BE = Φ, erecting Golden Rectangle AEFD.
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: Golden Rectangles, √5 Rectangles, & Whirling-Square Gnomonic Spirals
items.theorem_enunciation: Flanking a unit square ABCD on both sides via its base-midpoint circle produces a 1 × √5 rectangle WEFN containing right golden rectangle AEFD; recursive whirling-square cuts in gnomon BEFC share perpendicular main and secondary diagonals [AF] ⊥ [EC] (spread s = 1) meeting at pole P = (Φ²/√5, Φ/√5).
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: Golden Triangles (72°–72°–36°) & Golden Gnomons (36°–36°–108°)
items.theorem_enunciation: An isosceles acute golden triangle ABC with base AB = 1 and legs AC = BC = Φ is partitioned by base-angle bisector AD (with AD = CD = 1 and BD = φ) into an obtuse golden gnomon CAD and a self-similar acute golden triangle DAB with exact spreads s(36°) = (5 − √5)/8 and s(72°) = (5 + √5)/8.
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: Regular Pentagon, Pentagram, Decagon & Paper-Knot Pentagon
items.theorem_enunciation: The five diagonals of a regular pentagon of side 1 enclose a similar inner pentagon of side φ² and cut each diagonal in the geometric progression φ² : φ : 1 : Φ; furthermore, folding a flat uniform strip of width w into a tight overhand knot locks parallel trapezoid edges into an exact regular pentagon of side w sec 18°.
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: Kepler's Golden Right Triangle (1, √Φ, Φ) & Circle-Square Near-Quadrature
items.theorem_enunciation: A right triangle with side lengths (1, √Φ, Φ) has side quadrances (1, Φ, Φ²) simultaneously in geometric progression and Pythagorean sum 1 + Φ = Φ², satisfies cos θ = tan θ = 1/√Φ, and equates the perimeter 4√Φ of the square on leg √Φ with the circumference πΦ of the circle on diameter Φ to within 0.096%.
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: Penrose Kites & Darts (P2) and Thick & Thin Golden Rhombs (P3)
items.theorem_enunciation: A thick 72°–108° golden rhomb of side Φ divides at unit distance K along its long diagonal of length Φ² into a convex Penrose kite KBCD and a non-convex Penrose dart ABKD with exact area ratio Φ : 1, matching the Φ : 1 area ratio between thick (72°) and thin (36°) Penrose golden rhombs.
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: Exact Radical Sines, Cosines, Tangents & Spreads of 18°, 36°, 54°, 72°
items.theorem_enunciation: On the unit circle, cos 36° = sin 54° = Φ/2 and sin 18° = cos 72° = φ/2 differ by exactly 1/2 and multiply to 1/4, while the pentagonal spreads s(36°) = (5 − √5)/8 and s(72°) = (5 + √5)/8 form the quadratic roots of Wildberger's five-fold spread factor 16 s² − 20 s + 5 = 0.
items.knott_page_title: Exact Trig Values for Simple Angles
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: The Complete 3° Constructible Angle Lattice (3°k for k = 1..29)
items.theorem_enunciation: Superimposing pentagonal angles in Q(√5) with equilateral and half-right angles in Q(√2, √3) expresses sin(3°k), cos(3°k), tan(3°k), and spread s(3°k) in explicit nested square roots for all 29 acute multiples of 3°, while Gauss's Fermat prime 17 = 2⁴ + 1 extends compass constructibility to cos(π/17).
items.knott_page_title: Exact Trig Values for Simple Angles
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: Three Orthogonal Golden Rectangles → Regular Icosahedron & Dodecahedron
items.theorem_enunciation: Three mutually perpendicular 2 × 2Φ golden rectangles have 12 corners (0, ±1, ±Φ) forming a regular icosahedron of edge 2, volume 20Φ²/3, and rational dihedral spread 4/9, while (±1, ±1, ±1) ∪ cyc(0, ±φ, ±Φ) forms a regular dodecahedron of edge 2φ, volume 8 + 4Φ, and dihedral spread 4/5.
items.knott_page_title: The Golden Geometry of Solids or Phi in 3 Dimensions
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: Inscribed Cube & Compound of Five Cubes in a Dodecahedron
items.theorem_enunciation: Inside a regular dodecahedron of edge 2φ, the 60 face diagonals of length 2 = Φ · (2φ) partition into five congruent inscribed cubes of edge 2 and volume 8, with each of the 20 dodecahedral vertices belonging to exactly two cubes.
items.knott_page_title: The Golden Geometry of Solids or Phi in 3 Dimensions
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: Acute & Obtuse Golden Rhombohedra (3D Quasicrystal / Ammann Tiles)
items.theorem_enunciation: Triples of five-fold icosahedral vectors of quadrance Φ + 2 span acute (prolate) and obtuse (oblate) golden rhombohedra bounded by six congruent golden rhombi of diagonal ratio Φ : 1, with exact volumes 2Φ² and 2Φ in ratio Φ : 1 and 10 + 10 assembly into a rhombic triacontahedron of volume 20Φ³.
items.knott_page_title: The Golden Geometry of Solids or Phi in 3 Dimensions
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: Fibonacci Power Linearization (Φⁿ = FₙΦ + Fₙ₋₁) & The Phibonacci Brick
items.theorem_enunciation: Every integer power n ∈ Z of the Golden Ratio reduces to the linear form Φⁿ = Fₙ Φ + Fₙ₋₁ and (−φ)ⁿ = Fₙ₊₁ − Fₙ Φ = Fₙ₋₁ − Fₙ φ, while a rectangular Phibonacci brick of edges (1, φ, Φ) has unit volume 1, surface area 4Φ, and integer space diagonal 2.
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: Extremal Continued Fraction [1; 1, 1, …], Convergents Fₙ₊₁/Fₙ, & Nested Radicals
items.theorem_enunciation: The all-ones simple continued fraction Φ = [1; 1, 1, …] has rational convergents cₖ = Fₖ₊₁/Fₖ with exact alternating error cₖ − Φ = (−φ)ᵏ/Fₖ, saturating Hurwitz's irrationality constant √5 via :math:`F_k^2 |c_k - \Phi| \to 1/\sqrt{5}`.
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: Bergman's Base-Φ ('Phigit') Numeral System
items.theorem_enunciation: Under the carry law Φⁿ = Φⁿ⁻¹ + Φⁿ⁻² (100_Φ = 011_Φ), every positive integer N ≥ 1 admits a unique finite minimal non-adjacent {0, 1} expansion in powers of Φ; excluding infinite 011-tails yields a unique 00-free maximal form and exactly Fₖ valid finite phigit forms for every Fibonacci number Fₖ.
items.knott_page_title: Phigits and the Base Phi System
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: The Infinite Golden String (101101011011…), Rabbit Tree & Cutting-Line Slope φ
items.theorem_enunciation: Iterating the Rabbit substitution 1 ↦ 10, 0 ↦ 1 generates the infinite Sturmian Golden String dₙ = ⌊(n + 1)φ⌋ − ⌊nφ⌋, identically realized geometrically as the sequence of vertical ('1') and horizontal ('0') unit-lattice crossings of the ray y = φ x from the origin.
items.knott_page_title: The Fibonacci Rabbit Sequence (The Golden String)
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: Zeckendorf's Theorem (Canonical Fibonacci Base Representation)
items.theorem_enunciation: Every positive integer N ≥ 1 decomposes uniquely as a sum of non-consecutive Fibonacci numbers F_{k₁} + F_{k₂} + … + F_{kᵣ} (kᵢ ≥ kᵢ₊₁ + 2, kᵣ ≥ 2), producing a unique 11-free binary numeral in Fibonacci place values (…, 13, 8, 5, 3, 2, 1).
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: Wythoff's Array, Beatty's Complementary Sequences (⌊nΦ⌋, ⌊nΦ²⌋), & Stolarsky's Array
items.theorem_enunciation: Because 1/Φ + 1/Φ² = 1, Beatty's sequences Aₙ = ⌊nΦ⌋ and Bₙ = ⌊nΦ²⌋ = Aₙ + n partition Z_{>0} without overlap; seeding generalized Fibonacci rows via W(r, c) = ⌊(r + 1)Φ⌋ F_{c+2} + r F_{c+1} (Wythoff) or nearest-integer multiples [kΦ] (Stolarsky) places every positive integer in a unique (row, col) cell.
items.knott_page_title: General Fibonacci Series, Wythoff and Stolarsky Arrays
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: Fibonacci Generator of Primitive Pythagorean Triples
items.theorem_enunciation: Any four consecutive positive Fibonacci numbers (Fₙ, Fₙ₊₁, Fₙ₊₂, Fₙ₊₃) form the Pythagorean right triangle (Fₙ Fₙ₊₃, 2 Fₙ₊₁ Fₙ₊₂, F₂ₙ₊₃) of area Fₙ Fₙ₊₁ Fₙ₊₂ Fₙ₊₃ and inradius Fₙ Fₙ₊₁, primitive whenever 3 ∤ n and twice a primitive triple when 3 ∣ n.
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: Cassini's Identity (Fₙ₋₁Fₙ₊₁ − Fₙ² = (−1)ⁿ) & The 64 ↔ 65 / 63 Jigsaw Dissections
items.theorem_enunciation: Cassini's alternating identity Fₙ₋₁ Fₙ₊₁ − Fₙ² = (−1)ⁿ manifests geometrically when the four pieces of an 8 × 8 = 64 square (two 3 × 8 triangles and two 5 × (3, 5) trapezoids) rearrange into a 5 × 13 = 65 rectangle with a +1 parallelogram gap OR into a 63-unit notched block with a −1 parallelogram overlap.
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: Binet, Lucas, Catalan, d'Ocagne, Honsberger & Fibonomial Power Identities
items.theorem_enunciation: Binet's closed forms Fₙ = (Φⁿ − (−φ)ⁿ)/√5 and Lₙ = Φⁿ + (−φ)ⁿ place (Lₙ, Fₙ) on the alternating Pell-Lucas hyperbolas Lₙ² − 5 Fₙ² = 4(−1)ⁿ with unit sector triangles, unify Catalan, d'Ocagne, and Honsberger identities, and annihilate k-th powers Fₙᵏ via signed Fibonomial coefficients.
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: Fibonacci Arctangent Telescoping Formulae for π
items.theorem_enunciation: By Cassini's odd-index relation F₂ₙ₊₁² − 1 = F₂ₙ F₂ₙ₊₂, every even-indexed reciprocal Fibonacci angle splits as arctan(1/F₂ₙ) = arctan(1/F₂ₙ₊₁) + arctan(1/F₂ₙ₊₂), telescoping from arctan(1/F₂) = π/4 into Lehmer's series π/4 = ∑_{k=1}^∞ arctan(1/F₂ₖ₊₁).
items.knott_page_title: The Fibonacci Numbers in a Formula for Pi
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey

items.title: Golden Angle (360° / Φ² ≈ 137.50776°) & Parastichy Bridges
items.theorem_enunciation: Dividing a full turn in extreme and mean ratio yields the Golden Angle 2π / Φ² = 2π φ² ≈ 137.50776°, whose cylindrical primordia satisfy Fₖ φ² − Fₖ₋₂ = (−φ)ᵏ, pairing opposing left- and right-handed parastichy spirals in consecutive Fibonacci numbers (Fₖ, Fₖ₊₁).
items.copyright_attribution: © 1996–2025 Dr. Ron Knott, University of Surrey
